chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan al-Ruqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrah with Hajj (Tamattu'), entered Mecca, performed Tawaf and Sa'i, wore his clothes, and exited Ihram, but forgot to shorten (his hair/nails) until he went out to Arafat. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. He builds upon the Umrah and its Tawaf, and the Tawaf of the Hajj follows it.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.سَعَى: Performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.يَبْنِي: Builds upon / relies on (legal term for combining rituals)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (hair/nails), a ritual act ending Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to end Ihram before going to Arafat during Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting to shorten hair or trim nails before leaving Mecca for Arafat does not invalidate the Umrah of Tamattu'. The Imam rules that the pilgrim simply performs the Hajj Tawaf immediately following the Umrah Tawaf, demonstrating the Shia principle of ease (yusr) in ritual obligations when forgetfulness is involved. This ruling highlights the distinction between intentional violation and accidental omission in the jurisprudence of Hajj.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahimasws (7th Imamasws), from a man who performs Tumatto with the Umra to the Hajj. So he entered Makkah and performs Tawaaf, and performs Sa’ee, and he wore his clothes, and became free from Ihraam, and forgot that he should be shortening (hair, nails, etc.) until he went out to Arafaat. Heasws said: ‘There is not problem with it. He would build upon the Umra, and its Tawaaf, and Tawaaf of the Hajj upon its tracks’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous). He enters Makkah, performs Tawaf and Sa‘y between al-Safa’,’ al-Marwah. He then dresses up normally and comes out of the state of Ihram but forgets to do Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on) until he leaves for ‘Arafat. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. He continues upon his al-‘Umrah, its Tawaf and Tawaf of al-Hajj consequently.’”
